memory_update.text: VECO should be promoted as the cleanest US-listed underfollowed candidate for the node because it has direct InP MOCVD optical-communications laser order evidence.

AXTI should remain in the universe as a substrate-level InP/GaAs wafer candidate, but survival to later layers depends on verifying AI/datacom revenue mix, customer qualification and geopolitical/export-control risk.
MKSI is a broader second-order supplier candidate, best treated as a subsystem, photonics, optics, test and advanced-packaging exposure rather than a pure optical-epitaxy bottleneck.

The research chain to track is: hyperscaler AI networking demand -> optical modules/transceivers -> lasers/photonic components -> InP/GaAs wafers and qualified epitaxy capacity -> MOCVD/MBE/process tools and supporting photonics/test subsystems.

Need a focused follow-up search on US-listed optical test and certification-gate suppliers for 800G/1.6T, co-packaged optics, silicon photonics and laser burn-in because this pass found stronger evidence for tools and substrates than for independent test bottlenecks.

node: AI optical connectivity production chain: lasers, compound-semiconductor epitaxy, wafers, and epitaxy tools
summary: Layer 1B expands the US-listed universe around the upstream optical-connectivity bottleneck. The strongest underfollowed fit is Veeco as a direct MOCVD/InP epitaxy-tool supplier for optical communications lasers. AXT is a substrate-level InP/GaAs wafer candidate tied to data-center connectivity but requires verification of AI/datacom mix, customer concentration, and supply-chain durability. MKS is a second-order subsystem, photonics, test, optics, process-control, and packaging supplier that may benefit beneath semiconductor and photonics tool OEMs, but its exposure is broader and more indirect. Lumentum is included only as a higher-attention reference anchor at the laser/component layer to calibrate whether upstream tools and substrates are seeing AI-driven order pull-through.
